sources.population: Taiwan Biobank; 6184 men and 8353 women aged 30-70, recruitment described as 2012-2016; volunteer cohort, not U.S. probability sample.
sources.measurement: HDL-C in mg/dL from biobank biochemical examinations; detailed assay and fasting protocol not specified in this article. Table 2 reports mean plus SE, not SD.
sources.cohort_overlap: One Taiwan Biobank analysis. No overlap known with MIDUS or ALSPAC/MEIRU. Related Taiwan articles would not be independent confirmations.

sources.population: Urban Malawi MEIRU and predominantly White UK ALSPAC; adults 2277 Malawi and 6323 UK, plus adolescents. Adult UK women mean age 47.9 and men 53.3.
sources.measurement: Fasting enzymatic serum lipids in Malawi (Beckman AU480) and fasting plasma lipids in UK (Technicon RA500), mmol/L.
sources.cohort_overlap: ALSPAC parents and offspring share families. MEIRU and ALSPAC are distinct cohorts; article's related MEIRU work is overlapping, not independent.

sources.population: 1903 White and African American MIDUS biomarker participants, 860 men and 1043 women; 2004-2006 and 2011-2016 cohorts; ages 25-86 across cohorts. Biomarker volunteers more educated, Milwaukee African American oversampling; includes diabetes and medication use.
sources.measurement: 12-hour fasted blood; traditional clinical lipid panel in mg/dL at Meriter certified laboratory; source also studies HDL peroxide, a different endpoint not modeled here. Source used log HDL-C in analyses to normalize distribution.
sources.cohort_overlap: Two MIDUS biomarker cohorts pooled within one article, not two independent confirmations. No known overlap with other selected sources.

evidence.locator: Table 2, Sex rows; BMI definitions in Methods 2.2
evidence.estimand: Unadjusted HDL-C means and standard errors within sex and BMI category
evidence.adjustment: Stratified by sex and BMI category; not jointly age-adjusted
evidence.uncertainty: Reported SEs quantify mean uncertainty; category BMI means and age composition are unavailable. SE is not an individual residual SD.
evidence.applicability: Large adult sample supplies sex-stratified direction and scale, but category means conflate within-category covariates and cohort-specific selection.
evidence.model_use: Normal-to-obese mean ratio determines each sex's log-BMI slope at assumed representative BMI values. Other categories are checks, not fitted targets.

evidence.estimand: Adjusted additive HDL-C mean contrasts versus ages 30-40
evidence.adjustment: Model lists exercise, WHR, BMI category, body fat category, sex, age category, smoking, drinking, coffee and vegetarian diet; full design details/covariance unavailable
evidence.uncertainty: No coefficient SE or covariance reported. P-values are not residual variance. Printed age categories overlap at 40, limiting exact bin interpretation.
evidence.applicability: Evidence for modest nonmonotone age pattern in ages 30-70, conditional on more predictors than the generator possesses.
evidence.model_use: Piecewise-linear interpolation of log relative mean through assumed bin centers, flat outside extreme centers. Common across sexes.

evidence.locator: Results paragraphs following Fig. 1; Fig. 2 caption and Methods Statistical analysis
evidence.estimand: Qualitative assessment of adiposity-lipid association shape and population/sex heterogeneity

reported.description: Most associations across adiposity fifths were approximately linear; inverse BMI-HDL associations in all four sex/age groups; BMI-HDL associations stronger in UK than Malawi and adult UK women than men.

evidence.uncertainty: Numerical slopes and category-distribution tables are in a PDF supplement unsupported by gateway. One Results sentence labels a positive LDL-context coefficient HDL; this internally inconsistent sentence is not used.
evidence.applicability: Supports direction and warns against assuming universal coefficients, but cannot numerically calibrate this model or its curvature.
evidence.model_use: Context only; retain modest smooth monotonic BMI structure rather than invent threshold effects or extract graph pixels.

evidence.locator: Results, Descriptive statistics, paragraph beginning 'On average, men had lower HDL-C levels'
evidence.estimand: Sex-specific marginal arithmetic HDL-C mean and SD
evidence.uncertainty: SDs describe people, not mean uncertainty. Values rounded; sex-specific mean SEs can be approximated as SD/sqrt(n) but no precision weighting is used.
evidence.applicability: Contemporaneous U.S. adults with diabetes and medication use resemble eligibility better than a healthy volunteer-only reference, but selection, age, ethnicity and fasting differ.
evidence.model_use: Primary anchors for mean and marginal variance after model-based removal of age/BMI mean variation under an explicit source-distribution bridge.

evidence.locator: Table 2, n, Age (yrs.) and BMI rows
evidence.estimand: Sex/race/diabetes-stratum counts and marginal predictor means and SDs
evidence.adjustment: Stratified on sex, race and diabetes
evidence.uncertainty: Joint age-BMI distributions, within-stratum covariance, BMI support and all cross-moments missing; values rounded.
evidence.applicability: Supports a working source-moment calculation, not recovery of source microdata or exact source operator.
evidence.model_use: Weighted four-stratum normal marginal moment closure within sex; zero within-cell covariance assumed. No latent race or diabetes labels are assigned to target rows.

evidence.locator: Methods: Blood collection and clinical lab results; Statistical analyses; Strengths and limitations

reported.biomarker_selection: More educated than full MIDUS; African American recruitment concentrated in Milwaukee

evidence.uncertainty: Log transformation of marginal HDL does not establish conditional lognormal residuals. Assay harmonization with target direct serum HDL is not demonstrated.
evidence.applicability: Relevant to location, tails and transport; HDL-C distinct from HDLperox throughout extraction.
evidence.model_use: Motivates positive skewed family, with gamma sensitivity; no assay offset estimated.
